content.title: Carrie Anne Fleming, 'Supernatural' and 'iZombie' actress, dies at 51
content.text: Carrie Anne Fleming, a Canadian actress best known for her recurring roles in two long-running CW shows, Supernatural and iZombie, died on Feb. 26. She was 51. Fleming died on Feb. 26 of breast cancer complications, Entertainment Weekly has learned. "She died peacefully with her loved ones by her side," a representative for the actress said in a statement. "It was a great privilege to have known Carrie. She was a beautiful soul, inspiring, and above all, kind. She will be greatly missed." Fleming's Supernatural costar Jim Beaver was first to announce the news, sharing an emotional social media post accompanied by a photograph of the two actors together on set. "My friend, my lover, my bright light, my beautiful costar," Beaver captioned the March 2 post. "Carrie Anne Fleming, who played Bobby Singer's wife Karen on Supernatural died on Thursday, February 26, after confronting cancer for a long time. My heart is broken." Representatives for Beaver did not immediately respond to EW's request for comment. Born Aug. 16, 1974, in Digby, Bear River, Nova Scotia, Canada, Fleming appeared in more than 40 screen roles across her three-decade career. She made her debut with a role in the 1994 NBC TV movie Viper and next landed an uncredited role in the Adam Sandler golf comedy, Happy Gilmore. From there, she made one-off appearances on shows such as Secret Agent Man, Stargate SG-1 and The Dead Zone. In 2005, she landed a role in a Dario Argento-directed episode, "Jenifer," of the horror anthology series, Masters of Horror. Fleming played the titular role, in the episode revolving around a disfigured woman with cannibalistic tendencies. Fleming next appeared on such popular series as Smallville and The L Word before landing the role of Karen Singer on Supernatural. In her first appearance on the show, in its second season, Fleming had a one-off role as a dying nurse. She would later return to play Bobby's deceased wife, Karen, in the season five episode "Dead Men Don't Wear Plaid." Two seasons later, she reprised her role for the Bobby-centric episode, "Death's Door." Fleming later returned to the CW for 12 episodes of iZombie, the drama about a medical resident-turned-zombie who solves crimes. She played braid dealer Candy Baker. Get your daily dose of entertainment news, celebrity updates, and what to watch with our EW Dispatch newsletter. Fleming's additional roles include Continuum, Motive, UnREAL, and Supergirl. In the 2015 TV film The Unauthorized Full House Story — which followed the behind-the-scenes making of the hit sitcom — Fleming played the mother of Full House star Candace Cameron Bure. The actress also acted onstage in several BC productions, including Romeo and Juliet, Steel Magnolias, and Fame. Fleming is survived by her daughter, Madalyn Rose (Max). A memorial service for the actress will be announced at a later date.
